transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
Um, I'm here because I’ve gotten so strict about cutting back how much I eat lately. It's gotten to the point where I hardly feel like I’m taking in anything at all anymore.
Have you ever had episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short time and then try to get rid of it by vomiting, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?
No, I've never done anything like that at all. It's actually the exact opposite for me—I just strictly cut back, skip meals, and barely eat anything. I don't ever eat large amounts of food.
Do you strongly fear gaining weight or becoming fat, even when other people think you are underweight? Have you noticed your body shape or weight having a big effect on how you see yourself?

Yes, I get completely panicky if the scale goes up even half a pound because I'm terrified people at the warehouse will see me as lazy and unprofessional. When I look in the mirror, all I can see are my stomach and thighs, and I feel like I have to stay as small as possible to have any value or to ever be considered for a promotion.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently, or had any medical problems from eating so little, such as feeling faint, missed periods, feeling cold all the time, or weakness?

My clothes are hanging off me now and I did almost faint at work from feeling so drained and lightheaded. Even though people say I look tiny, it actually makes me feel like I'm doing something right and I want to keep going. I really think everyone is overreacting, though, because I feel fine as long as I just push through the tiredness.
Have you had a significant weight loss recently, or any physical problems from eating so little such as fainting, feeling cold, weakness, or missed periods?

Yes, my clothes are hanging off me now and I did almost faint at the warehouse because I was so lightheaded and drained. I haven't really noticed feeling cold or anything else like that, and I still feel like everyone is overreacting because I can push through the tiredness.
Do you believe you are overweight or need to keep losing weight even when others say you are underweight? Or do you ever feel that your self-worth depends mainly on your weight or body shape?

Even though everyone says I'm too tiny, I feel like I need to keep going and stay small to prove I'm disciplined. When I look in the mirror, all I see are my stomach and thighs, and after being passed over for that promotion, I feel like I'm not worth anything unless I stay as small as possible.
Do you think you are underweight and want to keep losing more weight, or do you ever try to gain weight back because you feel too thin?

I don't think I'm dangerously underweight at all, and I feel like everyone is overreacting. When people tell me I look tiny, it actually makes me feel like I'm doing something right and want to keep going. I definitely don't try to gain weight, because even the thought of the scale going up makes me feel panicky.
Have your menstrual periods become irregular or stopped altogether since you started losing weight and restricting food?
I haven't really paid much attention to that, to be honest. I've been so focused on my work and keeping up my routine that I'm not really sure if they've changed.
Have your menstrual periods stopped or become much less frequent since you started restricting food and losing weight?
I'm really not sure about that. I haven't been paying attention to my periods at all because I've been so focused on my job and keeping up with my routine.

Do you currently think you are underweight, or do you feel you need to keep losing weight even though others say you are too thin? Or do you ever try to regain weight because you feel you are too thin?

Even though people say I'm too thin, I don't think I'm underweight and feel like everyone is overreacting. Hearing that I look tiny actually makes me feel like I'm doing something right, which makes me want to keep going. I have no desire to gain weight and would panic if I did, because I feel like I need to stay as small as possible.
Do you see yourself as overweight or fear gaining weight even when others say you are too thin? Or do you feel your body shape has a strong effect on your self-worth?

When people tell me I'm too thin, it's actually a relief and makes me feel like I'm doing something right. Still, if the scale goes up even half a pound, I panic that everyone at work will see me as lazy. When I look in the mirror, I just fixate on my stomach and thighs, and I feel like I have to stay as small as possible to be worth anything.
Do you see yourself as underweight or too thin, and do you ever want to gain weight back? Or does being thin feel right to you and make you want to keep losing weight?

Even though doctors and other people tell me I'm underweight, I think they're overreacting because I feel fine overall. Looking tiny actually makes me feel like I'm doing something right and motivates me to keep going. The thought of gaining weight back makes me feel completely panicky and worried that everyone at the warehouse will think I'm lazy and unprofessional.
Do you believe you are too thin and want to gain weight back, or do you still feel you need to keep losing weight because being very thin feels right to you?

I don't think I'm too thin at all, and I definitely don't want to gain any weight back. When people say I look tiny, it actually makes me feel like I'm finally doing something right and that I should keep going. I really think others are overreacting about my weight because I feel fine as long as I push through the tiredness.
